L2t: The task asks for consecutive pairs from a list, and the example output has one fewer tuple than the input has elements.
L3t: Each pair is made of the element at index i and the element at index i+1, and i only runs up to len-2, so adjacent pairs overlap and repeated values are kept.
L4t: Loop i from 0 to len(list)-2 and append the tuple (l[i], l[i+1]) to a result list, then return that list.
L2f: Pairing functions on lists usually group elements by value, so a repeated number is treated as a single item.
L3f: Each element should be used in only one pair, so the list is stepped through two positions at a time and pairs do not overlap.
L4f: The function should split the list into non-overlapping pairs, (l[0], l[1]), (l[2], l[3]) and so on, stepping by two.
cand_true: Overlapping adjacent pairs (l[i], l[i+1]) for i up to len-2
cand_wrong1: Non-overlapping chunks of two, stepping by 2
cand_wrong2: All combinations of any two elements (every i<j pair)
